extraction.name: IFEval
extraction.description: Instruction-Following Eval (IFEval) is a straightforward and easy-to-reproduce evaluation benchmark for large language models. It focuses on a set of verifiable instructions and contains around 500 prompts, with each prompt containing one or more verifiable instructions.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Prompts were created through four steps: generating a set of base prompts with randomly selected verifiable instructions appended, using few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts, applying few-shot prompting to rephrase each prompt to increase diversity, and finally manually checking and editing the rephrased prompts one by one.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended to the end of each prompt.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A few-shot prompting based approach was applied to rephrase each prompt to increase the diversity of phrasing, followed by manual checking and editing of the rephrased prompts one by one.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Few-shot prompting was used to identify illogical prompts and remove them.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The capability of LLMs to accurately interpret and follow natural language instructions is crucial for the safety and reliability of their implementations. Discrepancies or misunderstandings in following instructions can lead to unintended outputs, which might have dire results, especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically; there always exist edge cases where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed. Additionally, the loose instruction-following verification process designed to reduce false negatives is likely to introduce false positives.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models.
